name: Dark Greyish Brown
lede: Dark Greyish Brown is a dim, olive-grey brown, ColorHub's library name for a darkened, greyed shade of [[brown]], and one of the more common dark colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A darkened, greyed brown
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark greyish" plus the parent color [[brown]] [1]. The library's record for this swatch draws on both Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912, plate XLV, and the ISCC-NBS Dictionary of Color Names of 1955, and our data computes its nearest 1955 block as olive gray [1]. Ridgway's plates survive only as scans of an aged, printed chart, so the hex value is an approximation of the original ink, not a measurement of it [1].

The closest named neighbors on file are [[grebe]] and [[pelican]], both almost indistinguishable from it, with [[pale-umber]] close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 2,726 of 23,781 paintings, about 11.46 per cent, more common than most of the library's named colors, as photographed [2]. It holds a fairly steady rate across every century on file, from medieval panels to the twentieth century, and peaks in a small sample of 1930s paintings [2]. Vilhelm Hammershøi has it in more than half of his sampled works, well above the archive's average [2]. These are computed color matches on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
